items.title: Optimizing cost and latency with Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
items.summary: Prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock can cut input token costs by up to 90% when you repeatedly send the same context to foundation models. This post walks through six practical prompt caching scenarios using the Converse API: message content, system prompt, tool definition, mixed TTL, tenant isolation, and LangChain integration.

items.title: Build an AI-powered product tagging system with Amazon SageMaker serverless model customization
items.summary: Manually tagging thousands of catalog products is slow and inconsistent. This walkthrough shows how to customize Qwen3-8B with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on Amazon SageMaker serverless model customization, then deploy it for asynchronous inference to build a cost-efficient product tagging system.

items.title: Announcing instance preference lists for Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now offers instance preference lists for training and processing jobs. Specify an ordered list of up to five instance types, and SageMaker AI automatically launches on the first type with available capacity, eliminating manual retry loops and capacity-watching scripts.

items.title: Abnormal AI: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agentic email security at scale
items.summary: Learn how Abnormal AI deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter as an ephemeral compute scratch pad for the agents behind its real-time email threat detection at billion-message scale, plus the sandbox design decisions and practical lessons for builders deploying Code Interpreter in production.

items.title: Manage end-user OAuth consent for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now offers a Consent portal, a managed web experience and session binding endpoint for AgentCore Gateway. This post walks through provisioning a portal, configuring GitHub and Slack authorization code grant targets, and the end-user consent flow, and shows how to review activity in AWS CloudTrail.

items.title: How Ninth Wave built AI-powered open finance onboarding on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Learn how Ninth Wave built Compass, a multi-agent AI onboarding assistant on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that validates bank APIs against Financial Data Exchange (FDX) standards, scores compliance, and compresses open finance onboarding from weeks to minutes while meeting SOC 2 and PCI DSS requirements.

items.title: The generative AI customization spectrum: From prompt engineering to custom models on AWS
items.summary: Pick the right generative AI customization approach on AWS with an 8-step decision framework, from prompt engineering and RAG to fine-tuning, continued pre-training, and Amazon Nova Forge. Start simple and escalate only when you must.

items.title: Automate replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick
items.summary: Foundation models made catalog-wide demand forecasting easy; the hard part is now acting on the forecast. This post builds a closed detect-decide-act loop on Databricks and Amazon Quick that reconciles demand surges against live supplier availability and places replenishment orders unattended, escalating to a human only when no supplier can cover a surge.

items.title: Monitoring production agent lifecycle with AWS DevOps Agent and AgentCore Evaluations
items.summary: Multi-agent systems fail in ways traditional monitoring misses. This post presents a dual-layer approach to monitoring production agents: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations for continuous quality scoring and AWS DevOps Agent for autonomous infrastructure investigation, shown on a four-agent airline reservation system.

items.title: Beyond the price per token: Choosing the right OpenAI model on Amazon Bedrock for your workload
items.summary: Comparing models on dollars per million tokens misses what production workloads actually pay for: outcomes. This post shares an open-source benchmarking harness that measures cost per correct answer, agent trajectory cost, and rubric-graded deliverable quality across OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock.
